units: <cite ref="Yoma 86b:12">Yoma 86ᵇ</cite> <he>ואם ש׳ בהן וכ׳</he> but if he committed the same sins again, he must confess them.
<cite ref="Yoma 86b:13">Ib.</cite> <he>כיון … וש׳ בה וכ׳</he> when a man commits a sin and repeats it, it appears to him permitted; <cite ref="Moed Katan 27b">M. Kat. 27ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 16b">Ib. 16ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 18a:14">Ber. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>אם קרית לא שָׁנִיתָ ואם שנית וכ׳</he> if thou hast read (studied), thou hast not repeated, and if thou hast repeated, thou hast not reviewed a third time, and if thou hast done so, they have not explained it to thee (v. <cite ref="Q02021"><he>פָּרַשׁ</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Sotah 9a:3-11">Sot. 9ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Malachi 3:6">Mal. III, 6</cite>) <he>לא … ושָׁנִיתִי לה וכ׳</he> I never struck a nation and had to do it a second time, but you, children of Israel, have not been consumed; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 825:2">Yalk. Deut. 825</cite>.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 825:2">Ib.</cite> <he>שהיה מכה … ולא שׁוֹנֶה לו</he> who used to strike a man once and no more (killed with one stroke).

<cite ref="Tosefta Tahorot 4:1">Tosef. Toh. IV, 1</cite> <he>אומר לו שיִשְׁנֶה</he> we say to him that he should do it again (when it will be seen whether it can be done without touching uncleanness); <he>אין שׁוֹנִין בטהרות</he> we must not try again for the purpose of deciding in matters of levitical cleanness; <cite ref="Niddah 5b:21">Nidd. 5ᵇ</cite> <he>אומרים לו שְׁנֵה ושונה</he> we say to him, do it again, and he does it again; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U01576"><he>שָׁנוּי</he></cite>; f. <he>שְׁנוּיָה</he> &c.
<cite ref="Megillah 31a">Meg. 31ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 19b:14">Ab. Zar. 19ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="U01387"><he>שָׁלַשׁ</he></cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: (denom. of מִשְׁנָה) to study the Mishnah; in gen. to study; to teach.
units: <cite ref="Megillah 28b">Meg. 28ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 73a:41">Nidd. 73ᵃ</cite> <he>כל השונה וכ׳</he> he who studies (reviews) traditional laws every day.
<cite ref="Megillah 32a:13">Meg. 32ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tractate Soferim 3:10">Treat. Sof’rim III, 10</cite> <he>השונה בלא זמרה</he> who studies (Mishnah and Gemarah) without chant.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 44a:14">B. Mets. 44ᵃ</cite> <he>שנית לנו … ותִשְׁנֶה לנו וכ׳</he> in thy earlier days thou taughtest us …, and again in thy old days, thou teachest us &c.?; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 52b">Ab. Zar. 52ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Eruvin 92a:3">Erub. 92ᵃ</cite> <he>וכי רבי לא שְׁנָאָהּ וכ׳</he> but if Rabbi has not taught that, whence could R. Ḥiyya have it?; <cite ref="Yevamot 43a:3">Yeb. 43ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 62a:42">Nidd. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>רבי לא שנה וכ׳</he> Rabbi has not taught this? whence &c.? <cite ref="Yevamot 108b:10">Yeb. 108ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>מי שש׳ זו לא ש׳ זו</he> he who taught this, has not taught that, i.e. the two clauses in the Mishnah are from different authors, v. <cite ref="V00072"><he>תַּבְרָא</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Chullin 85a:9">Ḥull. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>ראה רבי</he> … <he>ושְׁנָאָן וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>ושנאו</he>) Rabbi approved of the opinion of R. …, and embodied it in the Mishnah as the opinion of ‘the scholars’.

<cite ref="Pesachim 3b:3">Pes. 3ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 63b:10">Ḥull. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם יִשְׁנֶה אדם לתלמידו וכ׳</he> one should always teach his pupil the shortest way (use the briefest terms).
<cite ref="Chullin 81b">Ib. 81ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>לא שָׁנוּ אלא וכ׳</he> they have taught this only with regard to a case &c., i.e. this is meant only when &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab.
<cite ref="Niddah 22b:6">Nidd. 22ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>במחלוקת שנויה</he>, v. <cite ref="M00890"><he>מַחֲלוֹקֶת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 59a:18">Snh. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>ונִישְׁנֵית</he>, v. <cite ref="N00468"><he>נֹחַ</he></cite>.

Ḥull. 63ᵇ למה נִשְׁנוּ בבהמה וכ׳ why are the laws of clean and unclean animals repeated (in Deut.)? With reference to quadrupeds, on account of hassh’suʿah (Deut. XIV, 7, which is not found in Lev. XI, 4) &c., v. שְׁסוּעָה; Bekh. 6ᵇ; a. e.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 33b">B. Mets. 33ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 94b">B. Kam. 94ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>בימי רבי נשנית משנה זו</he> this Mishnah was taught (originated) in Rabbi’s days.
<cite ref="Berakhot 28a:1">Ber. 28ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="P00127"><he>עֵדוּת</he></cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:52">Lam. R. to I, 6</cite> <he>הַשְׁנֵינִי פרק וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="S01874"><he>קָרָא</he> II</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to repeat, to come a second time. Y. Snh. III, 21ᵇ bot. לְשַׁנּוֹת, v. טַעֲנָה.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 4:20">Num. R. s. 4<sup>20</sup></cite> <he>ולא שִׁינְּתָה</he>, v. <cite ref="U01387"><he>שָׁלַשׁ</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to change, vary, modify; to make a distinction.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 6:2">B. Mets. VI, 2</cite> <he>כל המְשַׁנֶּה ידיו וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="J00093"><he>יָד</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 92b:15">Snh. 92ᵇ</cite> <he>אפי׳ … לא יְשַׁנֶּה אדם את עצמו וכ׳</he> even in time of danger (persecution) a man must not change himself from (disguise the insignia of) his office.
<cite ref="Yevamot 65b:7">Yeb. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>מותר … לשנות וכ׳</he> one may modify (the report of a person’s utterances) in the interest of peace.

<cite ref="Yevamot 65b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>גדול … הקב״ה ש׳ בו וכ׳</he> peace is a great thing, for even the Lord modified (Sarah’s words) for its sake (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 18:12">Gen. XVIII, 12</cite> a.
<cite ref="Genesis 18:13">13</cite>). Y. Pes. IV, 30ᵈ top <he>אל תְּשַׁנּוּ מנהג וכ׳</he> change not the usage of your fathers &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48">Gen. R. s. 48</cite> <he>זה אחד … שׁשִׁינּוּ וכ׳</he> this is one of the things which they (the seventy translators) changed for king Ptolemee.

<cite ref="Shabbat 10b:7">Sabb. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם אל יְשַׁנֶּה אדם בנו בין הבנים</he> a man must never distinguish his son among his sons (favor one son more than the others); <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 84:20">Gen. R. s. 84</cite>.

<cite ref="Beitzah 30a:2">Bets. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>אם אי אפשר לשנות</he> if it is not possible to do the thing in a different manner (so as to be reminded that it is a Holy Day). Tanḥ. Nitsabim 3 <he>כבר</he> … <he>שלא אֲשׁנֶּה בכם וכ׳</he> I have sworn to you that I will not change my relation to you &c.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 589:9">Yalk. Mal. 589</cite> <he>מי שי׳ במי</he> which of us changed his conduct towards the other?; <he>המקום לא שי׳ בישראל</he> God has not changed his relation to Israel; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְשׁוּנֶּה</he>; f. <he>מְשׁוּנָּה</he>. Y. Taan. I, end, 64ᵈ <he>עורב יצא מש׳ מן הבריות</he> the raven came out of the ark looking different from all other creatures (black).
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 5:2">Shek. V, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="T00998"><he>רִצְפָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 56a:2">Sabb. 56ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="II Samuel 12:9">II Sam. XII, 9</cite>) <he>מש׳ רעה זו וכ׳</he> this evil deed is different from all &c. Ib. 156ᵇ <he>מיתה מש׳</he> a strange (unnatural, sudden) death; <cite ref="Sotah 35a">Sot. 35ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 9:3">Deut. R. s. 9</cite> <he>ראה אותו מש׳</he> he saw him (the angel of death) looking strange (excited); <he>מפני מה אתה מש׳</he> why art thou excited?
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 38a:12">Snh. 38ᵃ</cite> <he>בשלשה … מִשְׁתַּנֶּה מחבירו וכ׳</he> by three things one man is distinguishable from another: by his voice &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 10:4">Pes. X, 4</cite> (<cite ref="Pesachim 116a:8">116ᵃ</cite>) <he>מה נ׳ הלילה וכ׳</he> why is this night different from all other nights? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 71b:2">Snh. 71ᵇ</cite> [read:] <he>הואיל ונ׳ דינו ונִשְׁתַּנֵית מיתתו</he> because his (the proselyte’s) legal status is different, and the mode of capital punishment is different for him.
<cite ref="Shabbat 53b:18">Sabb. 53ᵇ</cite> <he>נִשְׁתַּנּוּ לו סדרי וכ׳</he> the order of nature had to be changed for him.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 19a:6">R. Hash. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>מה נִישְׁתַּנִּינוּ מכל וכ׳</he> wherein are we different from any other nation or tongue that you decree for us such hard decrees?; a. e.
